factual_claims.claim: The broader labor market has not experienced a discernible disruption since ChatGPT’s release 33 months ago.

Historical technological shifts in the workplace, such as the Industrial Revolution or the introduction of personal computing, have typically unfolded over multi-decade periods rather than short-term cycles.
The occupational mix by 2002 was at most around 7 percentage points different than it was in 1996.
The share of workers in the lowest, middle, and highest occupational exposure groups has remained stable at around 29%, 46%, and 18%, respectively, since ChatGPT's launch.
Unemployed workers were in occupations where, on average, 25 to 35 percent of tasks could be performed by generative AI.
Claude's usage is heavily dominated by computer and mathematical occupations, and arts and media occupations are also overrepresented.
The occupational mix for recent college graduates (ages 20-24) rarely deviates outside of the 30-33% range compared to older college graduates (ages 25-34).
The Information, Financial Activities, and Professional and Business Services sectors have seen larger shifts in the job mix compared to the aggregate labor market.
